name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.174.0 — Review close re-stamps the build ledger row's deviations count from the sidecar's final entry count. The build driver writes that count at COMMIT, so a sidecar restated into countable bullets afterwards left the row permanently under-reporting (specs/20260912/14 recorded 0 against two real entries); the count is only final once the fold happens, which is the close. The correction rewrites the last build row for that spec in place, touching only the number, and prints itself once in the step that follows the close. 7.173.0 — The design review page's whole-product waiting line is fixed on three counts: the singular now reads "1 whole-product note still blocks sign-off" (the verb inflects with the count, in the server render, the in-page recount, and the chrome mock alike); the line is now served hidden whenever whole-product notes are open rather than omitted while the journey still has its own open items, so resolving that last scoped note reveals the warning in place instead of silently enabling sign-off until a reload; and five tests now pin the served shown/hidden/absent states and recount()'s show, hide and text branches, replacing the zero live coverage left behind when specs/20260912/07's cases expired at close. 7.172.0 — Client request lifecycle, four defect fixes (q240): POST /client/__notes/reopen now refuses 409 once design/mocks/status.json carries marks.approved — the same sign-off cut-off /client/__walk/exclusion already enforces — so a stale client tab can no longer un-withdraw a request after sign-off and let the next materialize retire the exclusion row derived from it; the request cards' "Put it back" control is omitted from every surface once approved, and ships hidden on an open request so the withdraw handler can reveal it; walk.browser.js's withdraw handler now paints the full withdrawn shape a reload renders (data-resolution, the withdrawn sentence, withdraw gone, putback revealed) instead of the bare word "Closed", and the exclusion row's putback handler drops its own row (dropped verdict, verdict buttons and "Change answer" gone, the dropped sentence activated from the section's new data-said-dropped) instead of leaving live verdicts on a claim that just went away; waiveNote stamps resolution: 'waived' so a seven-day-silence close renders its own sentence rather than the bare "Closed"; and viewer.css's .wk-home/.wk-more/.wk-j-cta/.wk-req-link gain the '.wk ' ancestor prefix that beats '.wk a { color: inherit }', the same specificity defect specs/20260912/06 D9 fixed on the review page.
